newsitem.title: DENMARK: British Airways Sun Air cancels Danish route.
newsitem.headline: British Airways Sun Air cancels Danish route.

text.p: British Airways Danish franchise partner Sun-Air said on Friday it requested permission from the mid-Jutland authorities to withdraw its Skive-Copenhagen domestic route due to insufficient load factors.
"Sun-Air attempted to offer passengers in mid-Jutland extra flight frequencies at competitive rates, but the initiative was countered by SAS and Cimber Air," Sun-Air said in a statement.
"Sun-Air has come to the conclusion that there is no demand for further flight connections between Skive and Copenhagen," it said.
Sun-Air said it planned to concentrate on other routes out of mainland Jutland, increasing existing capacity to meet major demand on flights from Billund and Aarhus.
In May 1996, British Airways signed a franchise deal with Sun-Air designed to increase global ticket sales and dent the regional dominance of Scandinavian Airlines System(SAS).
Sun-Air operates flights from Copenhagen and Aarhus to Oslo, Gothenburg, Stockholm and New York. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
